def min_couriers(packages):
    """
    Couriers move along an infinite number line at speed 1 (travelling from
    position x to position y takes exactly abs(x - y) time units).

    packages is a list of triples (s, a, b) of integers: package i becomes
    available for pickup at position a at time s, and must then be carried
    directly to position b, arriving (and completing) at time s + abs(a - b).
    A courier may pick up a package only if it is standing at position a at
    time s; arriving earlier and waiting is allowed.  Each package is handled
    by exactly one courier, and a courier carries at most one package at a
    time.  Every courier may initially appear at any position at time 0, so
    any single package on its own is always serviceable.  Consequently one
    courier can handle package j immediately after package i if and only if

        s_i + abs(a_i - b_i) + abs(b_i - a_j) <= s_j.

    Return the minimum number of couriers needed to deliver all packages.

    Constraints:
      * 0 <= len(packages) <= 100
      * -10**6 <= s, a, b <= 10**6 and s >= 0 for every triple
      * all triples are pairwise distinct
      * a == b is allowed (a zero-length delivery: a courier must simply be
        at position a at time s)

    The answer is a single int.  An empty list needs 0 couriers.

    Note: sizes are small, but assigning packages greedily in time order is
    not optimal in general; an exact combinatorial argument is required.

    >>> min_couriers([])
    0
    >>> min_couriers([(0, 0, 5), (10, 6, 3)])
    1
    >>> min_couriers([(0, 0, 5), (2, 0, 5)])
    2
    >>> min_couriers([(0, 0, 2), (0, 10, 12), (5, 3, 0), (14, 9, 10)])
    2
    """
